'''''Rumohra adiantiformis''''', the '''leather fern''' or '''leatherleaf fern''',<ref name=grin>[https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?409792 U.S. National Plant Germplasm System; GRIN-Global Web v 1.9.7.1: Taxonomy profile of ''Rumohra adiantiformis'']</ref><ref name=gil>Gilman, E. F. [http://hort.ifas.ufl.edu/database/documents/pdf/shrub_fact_sheets/rumadia.pdf ''Rumohra adiantiformis''.] Fact Sheet FPS-515. University of Florida Cooperative Extension, IFAS. 1999.</ref> is a [[species]] of [[fern]] in the wood fern [[family (botany)|family]] [[Dryopteridaceae]]. It has a wide distribution, mainly in the tropical Southern Hemisphere.

==Names==
Other common names include '''leathery shieldfern''',<ref>[http://www.dpiw.tas.gov.au/inter.nsf/Attachments/LJEM-7CV782/$FILE/Rumohra%20adiantiformis%20Notesheet.pdf ''Rumohra adiantiformis''.] Flora of Tasmania.</ref> '''iron fern''',<ref>[http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=RUAD ''Rumohra adiantiformis''.] USDA PLANTS.</ref> '''7-weeks-fern''',<ref name=de>De Souza, G. C., et al. (2006). [http://www.ufrgs.br/pgdr/arquivos/513.pdf An ethnobiological assessment of ''Rumohra adiantiformis'' (samambaia-preta) extractivism in Southern Brazil.] ''Biodiversity & Conservation'' 15(8), 2737-46.</ref> and '''climbing shield fern'''.<ref>[http://collections.tepapa.govt.nz/Taxon.aspx?irn=11565 ''Rumohra adiantiformis''.] Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, Wellington.</ref>

==Description==
Growing to {{convert|90|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall and broad, ''Rumohra adiantiformis'' is a bushy, tufted evergreen plant with glossy dark green [[frond]]s. These contain round [[Sorus|sori]] (reproductive clusters) on the underside of the [[Pinnate|pinnae]] (leaflets) unlike many other ferns which have separate specialized reproductive fronds. Many of the sori have protective [[Leaf shape|peltate]] [[Sorus|indusia]] (films), and prominent scales on the [[stipe (botany)|stipe]]s of the fronds.

==Distribution==
''Rumohra adiantiformis'' is native to South America, the Caribbean, southern Africa, the Western Indian Ocean islands, Papua New Guinea, and Australasia.<ref name=grin/> Countries it is native to include such diverse places as Brazil and Colombia,<ref>Gonzalez Castiblanco, G. P. 2004. [http://www.javeriana.edu.co/biblos/tesis/ingenieria/tesis151.pdf Factibilidad de exportacion de follaje de helecho de cuero (''Rumohra adiantiformis'') para ramos o adornos frescos.] Pontificia Universidad Javeriana, Bogota, Colombia, Facultad de Ingenieria, 134 pages.</ref> the Galápagos Islands,<ref>Wiggins, I. L. ''Flora of the Galápagos Islands''. Stanford University Press. 1971. 998 pages {{ISBN|0-8047-0732-4}}, {{ISBN|978-0-8047-0732-9}}</ref> the Greater Antilles in the Caribbean, Zimbabwe and South Africa<ref name=grin/> Australia, and New Zealand.

==Ecology==
An example of plant associations of ''Rumohra adiantiformis'' is found in the [[Westland temperate forests|Westland podocarp/broadleaf forests]] of New Zealand, with [[Phytocoenosis|flora associates]] including ''[[Ascarina lucida]]'', ''[[Pseudowintera colorata]]'', ''[[Neopanax colensoi]]'', ''[[Alsophila smithii]]'', and ''[[Blechnum discolor]]''.<ref>Hogan, C. M. 2009. [http://www.globaltwitcher.com/artspec_information.asp?thingid=95431 Crown Fern: ''Blechnum discolor''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213134120/http://www.globaltwitcher.com/artspec_information.asp?thingid=95431 |date=2012-02-13 }} Globaltwitcher.com, ed. N. Stromberg.</ref>

==Cultivation==
The fern is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] for [[groundcover]] and in [[floristry]].<ref name=gil/> As it is a tropical plant with only limited protection against frost, in [[temperate climate]]s it is normally grown under glass as a houseplant.
In the UK it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web 
| url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/21448/i-Rumohra-adiantiformis-i/Details 
| title = Rumohra adiantiformis | access-date = 11 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web 
| url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 
| page = 93 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 11 October 2018}}</ref>

It is of economic importance in [[Brazil]], where thousands of people generate their income by wild-harvesting and selling the fronds for use in flower arrangements.<ref name=de/>

==Conservation status==
This plant has been classified by the [[Department of Conservation (New Zealand)|New Zealand Department of Conservation]] as being "Not Threatened" under the [[New Zealand Threat Classification System]].<ref name="de Lange2024">{{CiteQ|Q130392985}}</ref>
